newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV TAKES REVENGE WITH WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV TAKES REVENGE WITH WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Russian swimming star Denis Pankratov, denied of two world records because of a dope test fiasco in Paris last year, took a brilliant revenge by setting a world record at the same World Cup meeting on Saturday.
Double Olympic champion Pankratov set his third short-course world record in just a week when he clocked 23.35 seconds in the 50 metres butterfly.
Pankratov beat the previous best mark of 23.45 set by Briton Mark Foster in December 1995 in Sheffield, England.

The Russian had warmed up for the Paris World Cup final in style by setting two world records, 51.93 seconds for the 100 metres butterfly on Wednesday in Imperia, Italy, and one minute 52.64 seconds in the 200 butterfly last Saturday in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.

At last year's World Cup final in the French capital, he had broken both the 100 metres and 200 metres butterfly short-course records only to be denied the marks because organisers had run out of bottles to administer the dope tests necessary for ratification.
"It was programmed like that," said Pankratov when asked about his three world records in quick succession. "With those three records, I make history.
"I was hurt by what happened last year," he added, referring to the dope test blunder. "You can't forget that kind of thing."
Pankratov is the first man to hold all four butterfly world records since Michael Gross -- 100 and 200 long-course (50-metre pool) and short-course (25-metre pool).

He was not the only one to shine in Paris as in-form Dutchman Marcel Wouda bettered the shortcourse world record he had set just last week by swimming a 400 metres individual medley in 4:05.41 seconds.

The 24-year-old Wouda, who had set the previous best mark of 4:05.59 last Saturday in Gelsenkirchen, just missed out on a medal at last year's Olympics but picked up three titles at the European sprint championships in December.
German Mark Warnecke had earlier broken his own 50 metres breaststroke shortcourse world record in 26.97 seconds. Warnecke, 26, is the reigning 100 metres breaststroke shortcourse world champion.

To cap a fine day for Germany, Warnecke's compatriot Joerg Hofmman broke the 400 freestyle shortcourse European record in 3:40.58, bettering his own best mark of 3:40.78 set last Saturday in Gelsenkirchen.
